name: Cerebellar Ataxia with Neuropathy and Bilateral Vestibular Areflexia Syndrome
aliases: Cerebellar Ataxia Neuropathy Vestibular Areflexia Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of progressive cerebellar ataxia confirmed by clinical examination and neuroimaging
Evidence of sensory neuronopathy or sensory neuropathy on nerve conduction studies and clinical assessment
Bilateral vestibular areflexia demonstrated by absent vestibulo-ocular reflex on head impulse testing or caloric testing
Presence of biallelic expansions in the RFC1 gene (if available)
Exclusion of alternative causes of ataxia, neuropathy, and vestibular dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (cerebellar ataxia, sensory neuropathy, and bilateral vestibular areflexia) must be present for diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation via RFC1 repeat expansion testing is supportive but not mandatory.

searchTerms: muscle weakness in hands or feet
loss of nerve insulation causing weakness

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; exclusion of other ataxia causes
RFC1 gene biallelic intronic AAGGG repeat expansion detected by molecular genetic testing
imaging: MRI brain showing cerebellar atrophy, predominantly vermian
Vestibular testing (video head impulse test, caloric testing) showing bilateral vestibular areflexia
other: Nerve conduction studies demonstrating sensory neuronopathy with reduced or absent sensory nerve action potentials
Vestibular evoked myogenic potentials (VEMP) often absent or reduced

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of cardiomyopathy and diabetes mellitus
Genetic testing positive for FXN gene mutations
Presence of autonomic failure with urinary incontinence
MRI showing pontine and cerebellar atrophy with hot cross bun sign

redFlags: Rapidly progressive ataxia with early autonomic failure
Presence of systemic features suggesting alternative diagnosis (e.g., malignancy, infection)
references: Cortese A, et al. Cerebellar ataxia, neuropathy, and vestibular areflexia syndrome due to RFC1 repeat expansions. Brain. 2019.
Szmulewicz DJ, et al. CANVAS: Cerebellar Ataxia with Neuropathy and Vestibular Areflexia Syndrome. Front Neurol. 2020.
Orphanet: Cerebellar ataxia with neuropathy and bilateral vestibular areflexia syndrome (ORPHA:504476).
